$comment: PRD section 12. Each pair of nations is at war or peace, with a tension 0 to 100. Monthly: historical events fire on their dates, tension drifts toward the pair's base in peace (and wears down toward warSettle in war) with some noise, then high tension may tip peace into war and low tension war into peace. Pirates are at war with everyone and don't appear here. 1660 opens with Spain at war with England in the Caribbean: whatever was signed in Europe, there was 'no peace beyond the line'. France is at peace with Spain until the War of Devolution (May 1667). The Treaty of Madrid (1670) brings England and Spain to terms. Piracy pressure rises with every merchant pirates take from a nation and decays monthly; above plague it makes news. A letter of marque costs price, less with standing, and is free at freeAt; legal attacks earn standing with the issuer. Governors pay bounties per ship (pirates scaled up by their nation's piracy pressure).

events.$comment: Treaty of Madrid: Spain recognises English Jamaica

flag.$comment: A new career picks a flag: it starts at that nation's capital, with 'standing' there (its governors know the captain).

missions.$comment: Governors' missions (docs/design/governor-missions.md). Each governor offers one a week; the captain keeps up to 'open' at once, and one not done lapses after 'lapseWeeks' with no penalty. Done, the governor who gave it pays into the captain's purse (it is his money, not plunder: bounties stay the crew's chest), and its merit counts with his nation as for standing. Hunt: a named pirate haunting the waters about a port within 'areaTiles' of his town, in the class of 'classes' whose strength (men times one and a tenth a gun) comes nearest the flagship's times 'match', 'crew' of her berths manned; she pays 'rewardShare' of her class's price (at least 'minReward'). Courier: a letter to a governor of a friendly town 'tiles' away, and his reply brought back: 'goldPerTile' each way (at least 'minReward'), 'advance' of it paid by the governor the letter is handed to, the rest by the one who gave it when the reply is brought back; the chart rings the port the letter (then the reply) is bound for, 'ringTiles' about it.

news.war: {nation} and {other} are at war! Their ships are fair game to each other's privateers.
news.peace: {nation} and {other} have made peace. Letters of marque between them no longer hold.
news.plague: Pirates plague the {nation} trade. {nation} governors pay well for every pirate taken.
news.aiTaken: The {nation} {ship} was taken by pirates off {town}.
news.aiPirateSunk: The pirate {ship} was sent to the bottom by a {other} ship off {town}.
news.warPrize: The {nation} {ship} was taken by a {other} ship off {town}.
news.hoardDug: {captain}'s buried hoard has been dug up on the coast near {town}. Someone sails richer for it.
news.famousHunts: {captain} has sworn to take the captain whose name is on every tongue. He means to hunt them down.
news.famousRevenge: {captain} swears revenge on whoever dug up his hoard near {town}. He means to hunt them down.
news.famousBeaten: {captain} was beaten off {town}. They say he has gone to ground and his crew have scattered.

ranks.$comment: Ranks per nation (slice 8 of docs/design/combat-model.md, after Pirates! 2004): a letter of marque is the first rung; merit with a nation (each deed its governor pays a bounty for, a famous pirate handed over counting 'bountyStanding' as for standing) raises the captain up the 'ladder' while he holds its letter. Each rung brings something new at that nation's ports, from the rung named in 'perks' up: recruits at 'recruit' of the price (captain), repairs at 'repair', the shipwright's city-only fits at its towns too and upgrades at 'upgrade' (major), 'price' better on every trade (colonel; its capital's yard builds him a frigate), and its governors sell him estates (admiral: 'estate.acres' acres a lot, the first for 'estate.gold' and each lot after, in any nation, 'estate.rise' times the last, so gold has something to buy late in a career that grows dearer as it goes); a title ('acres' on the rung, baron and up) brings land that pays 'rentPerAcre' gold a month and grows 'acresPerMerit' for each merit past the first title.

career.$comment: Fame and the retirement score (slice 8). Three fames (after Uncharted Waters), from the career's record: trade (from the gold made trading: the first point at 'trade.goldStep', each after it 'trade.goldStep' dearer than the last, so the tenth comes at 55 steps), war (a point a prize, a point a pirate beaten, 'war.famous' a famous pirate beaten) and adventure ('adventure.hoard' a hoard dug up, 'adventure.mapPiece' a piece of a map held). The score sums the fames, his wealth (the gold to his name, on the same rising ladder by 'score.goldStep': a fortune counts, but a second fortune counts for less than the first, so no one way of playing wins it alone), a point every 'score.acresPer' acres, and each nation's rank (score.rank, by rung, marque first), times the difficulty level's 'score'. Retiring in port ends the career; 'fates' names what became of him, the highest whose score he reached.
